title: Exponential-Wrapped Mechanisms: Differential Privacy on Hadamard Manifolds Made Practical
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: Our mechanism yields consistently lower estimation error than the baseline across geometries, dimensions, and privacy levels, especially at strong privacy.
layout: 3x3 grid of line plots, rows by metric, columns by dimension, shared legend
description: A 3x3 grid of line plots comparing two differentially private mechanisms, EWG (red, circle markers) and RL (blue, triangle markers). Each row is a different SPD-matrix metric: Affine-Invariant, Log-Euclidean and Log-Cholesky. Each column is a different matrix dimension d, such as 3, 10, 15, or 6 in one case. The x-axis is the privacy parameter mu, from about 0.1 to 2. The y-axis is Riemannian distance, which measures error. Shaded bands show variability around each line. In every panel, error falls steeply as mu grows. The blue RL curve starts much higher and has a wider band than the red EWG curve, particularly at small mu. The two curves converge at large mu. The eye goes first to the tall blue spikes at the top left of each panel. Legends sit in the upper right of each panel.

abstract: We propose a general and computationally efficient framework for achieving differential privacy (DP) on Hadamard manifolds, which are complete and simply connected Riemannian manifolds with non-positive curvature. Leveraging the Cartan-Hadamard theorem, we introduce Exponential-Wrapped Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms that achieve $\epsilon$-DP, $(\epsilon, \delta)$-DP, Gaussian DP (GDP), and Rényi DP (RDP) without relying on computationally intensive MCMC sampling. Our methods operate entirely within the intrinsic geometry of the manifold, ensuring both theoretical soundness and practical scalability. We derive utility bounds for privatized Fréchet means and demonstrate superior utility and runtime performances on both synthetic data and real-world data in the space of symmetric positive definite matrices (SPDM) equipped with three different metrics. To our knowledge, this work constitutes the first unified extension of multiple DP notions to general Hadamard manifolds with practical and scalable implementations.
